subclaims.reason: discard() (celery/utils/collections.py:613) and re-add via add() (celery/utils/collections.py:572-576) remove the _data entry but leave the old heap entry behind. purge() peeks at the heap top without skipping stale entries (celery/utils/collections.py:633) and calls pop() whenever that stamp looks expired (celery/utils/collections.py:634-636). pop() skips heap entries whose item is absent from _data and evicts the next present item (celery/utils/collections.py:640-647), so a stale expired entry triggers eviction of a live unexpired item. A stale entry for a re-added key is worse: pop() never compares stamps, so it evicts the live re-added entry (celery/utils/collections.py:643). The sequence is single-threaded and deterministic: add('a',0), discard('a'), add('b',100), purge(now=100) with expires=10 evicts unexpired 'b'. The 15% heap-refresh guard (celery/utils/collections.py:550-553) does not run on this path and does not prevent one stale entry.
